clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A client recovering from orthopedic surgery is learning how to care for the surgical wound at home. Which statement shows correct understanding?

options.A: I will clean my hands before and after wound care and ask family or visitors not to touch the incision or dressing.
options.B: I need hand hygiene around the wound only when the dressing is visibly soiled or drainage is present.
options.C: Family members may touch the incision or dressing without cleaning their hands if they do not feel ill.
options.D: Gloves replace hand hygiene, so healthcare workers do not need to clean their hands before examining the wound.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current CDC Surgical Site Infection Basics instructs patients to clean their hands before and after caring for a surgical wound. CDC also states that family and friends should not touch the surgical wound or dressings and should clean their hands before and after visiting. Healthcare providers should clean their hands as well. These recommendations apply even when the wound or dressing is not visibly soiled. Therefore option A demonstrates correct infection-prevention teaching.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Prevent postoperative wound contamination through hand hygiene before and after wound care and by avoiding unnecessary contact with the incision or dressing.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
semantic_correction.source_version_date: April 11, 2024; current CDC page accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: After surgery — family and friends should not touch the surgical wound or dressings; family and friends should clean their hands before and after visiting; always clean your hands before and after caring for your wound; ask healthcare providers to clean their hands
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: CDC directly recommends hand hygiene before and after surgical-wound care and avoiding visitor contact with the wound or dressings as postoperative SSI-prevention measures.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'only' distractor cue, shortened the correct answer, and anchored home wound-care teaching to current CDC hand-hygiene and no-touch recommendations.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests source-supported postoperative wound contamination prevention and remains distinct from Q1863, which tests recognition of infection signs.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches CDC recommendations for hand hygiene before/after wound care and avoiding visitor contact with the wound or dressing.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. CDC recommends hand hygiene before and after wound care regardless of visible soil or drainage.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Visitors should clean their hands and should not touch the wound or dressings.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Healthcare workers should clean their hands; glove use does not replace indicated hand hygiene.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone matches the current CDC postoperative wound-care prevention recommendations.
cueing_check: All four choices are wound-care prevention statements of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
